title: High-school student
who: Class 11–12, studying for exams and school projects
mindset: Use AI as a tutor, not an answer machine: ask it to explain, quiz you and check your reasoning.

items.why: Turn on Study mode so it walks you through problems step by step instead of handing you the answer.
Guided Learning breaks a topic into small steps and checks your understanding as you go.
Ask it to explain a concept 'like I'm in class 11', then to quiz you with 5 questions.
Upload your notes and textbook chapters to get flashcards, quizzes and audio summaries based only on your material.
For projects: answers with sources you can open, check and cite.

items.name: Khanmigo
items.why: Khan Academy's AI tutor, designed for students and built not to just give answers away.
Ask it to build a small interactive simulation of a physics or chemistry idea, then play with the variables.
Turn a school project into a real website by describing it.

watchOut: Copy-pasting AI answers into homework skips the learning and is easy for teachers to spot. Never trust a fact, formula or citation until you've checked it.

title: Frontend developer
who: Building web UIs with React, Vue, Svelte or plain HTML/CSS
mindset: Let agents produce the first 80% of the UI, and spend your time on taste, accessibility and edge cases.

items.why: Works across your whole repo: builds components, wires state and runs your tests.
If you prefer staying in an editor: inline completion plus an agent panel.
Feeds current docs for your exact framework version, so you get fewer outdated APIs.
The frontend-design skill steers the agent away from the generic AI look toward a deliberate design.
The agent reads real frames, variables and components instead of guessing from a screenshot.
Components that models generate well, and the code lives in your repo.
The agent can inspect DOM, console, network and performance to fix what it built.
Check every breakpoint at once before you ship AI-generated layouts.
Pull an existing brand's tokens into Tailwind or shadcn so new pages match it exactly.
Brings WCAG, button-state and type-scale rules into every change the agent makes.
Deliberate motion and micro-interactions, with a plan you approve before code.
Have the agent write and run end-to-end tests against the real browser.

watchOut: AI-generated UI often misses focus states, keyboard navigation and contrast. Review accessibility yourself, or with a skill, before merging.

title: UX / UI designer
who: Research, flows, visual design and design systems
mindset: Use AI to explore more directions and test ideas faster. Judgment, research and taste stay your job.

items.why: Generate several UI directions from a prompt or sketch, then export to Figma.
Synthesize interview transcripts with citations back to what users actually said.
Draft personas, journey maps and UX copy variants to react to.
Turn a flow into a clickable prototype you can test with real users today.
Hand off designs that coding agents implement faithfully, down to variables and components.
Audit a competitor's or client's design system in seconds: colors, type and spacing.
Run Nielsen-heuristic and WCAG 2.2 reviews with an agent that cites the rule it applies.
Ship small production changes yourself, starting from your own Figma file.
Turn motion intentions into an approved interaction plan, then working code.

watchOut: Generated screens are not research. Don't paste confidential user data into tools your company hasn't approved.

title: Backend / AI engineer
who: Adding AI features to products and services
mindset: Start with the simplest thing: one prompt plus evals. Add RAG, tools and agents only when the evals show you need them.

items.why: Try several models behind one key before you commit to a provider.
Validated, typed output from day one, with no brittle string parsing.
Trace every call, its cost and latency from the first prototype.
Prompt and model regression tests in CI.
RAG over your data once prompting alone isn't enough.
Vector search in the Postgres you already run.
Expose your service to every AI client as an MCP server.
Durable, controllable agents with human approval steps.
Run code your agent writes in an isolated sandbox.
One gateway with budgets, keys and fallbacks across providers.
Scan for prompt injection and jailbreaks before launch.

watchOut: Without evals you can't tell whether a change helped. Treat all retrieved content and tool output as untrusted input.

title: Biotech / life-science researcher
who: Wet lab, computational biology or drug discovery
mindset: General assistants for reading and writing, domain models for structures, coding agents for analysis. Verify everything against primary data.

items.why: Literature reviews that search papers and extract methods, results and sample sizes into a table.
Ask questions across the papers you upload, with citations to the exact passage.
Predict protein and complex structures in a browser, free for non-commercial research.

items.name: Claude for Life Sciences
items.why: Connectors to research tools such as Benchling and PubMed, plus skills for common scientific workflows.
Keep analysis reproducible: code, data and figures in one notebook.
Have an agent write and run your analysis scripts and notebooks, so you review code, not copy-pasted numbers.
Open structure and binding-affinity models you can run in-house and use commercially.
Run Boltz or other models on serverless GPUs without managing a cluster.
Connect your lab's databases or ELN to agents through a custom MCP server.

watchOut: Never paste unpublished or patient data into consumer chat apps. Treat AI summaries of papers as leads, not facts, and check the figure or table yourself.

title: Non-technical professional
who: Product, marketing, operations, HR or finance
mindset: Automate the repetitive parts of your week, and keep people on the decisions.

items.why: Draft documents, analyze spreadsheets and summarize long threads.
Brainstorm, rewrite and use voice mode for thinking out loud.
Quick market and competitor research with sources.
Turn policy docs and reports into a Q&A notebook for your team.
The docx, xlsx and pptx skills produce real, formatted Office files, not just text.
Connect AI to Gmail, Slack and Sheets to automate recurring workflows.
Build an internal chatbot over your team's documents, with no code.
Prototype the internal tool you've always wanted, by describing it.

watchOut: Don't automate decisions that affect people without review. Don't connect AI to accounts with more access than the task needs.
